message.content:
Sure! To generate a 5‑second audio clip at 440 Hz you would use the **`generate_sound_wave`** function.  
Here’s the function signature and a quick example of how to call it:

```python
// Function signature
generate_sound_wave({
    frequency: number,          # Frequency in Hz (e.g., 440)
    duration: number,           # Duration in seconds (e.g., 5)
    wave_type?: "sine" | "square" | "sawtooth",  # Optional; defaults to "sine"
})
```

### Example call

```python
result = generate_sound_wave({
    frequency: 440,
    duration: 5,
    wave_type: "sine"   # optional – omitted will also work
})

// `result` typically contains the path or identifier of the created .wav file
print("Generated file:", result)
```

This will create a WAV file containing a pure sine wave at 440 Hz lasting 5 seconds. You can then play it back using the `play_sound_wave` function if needed.
